motions.item_title: Adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming November 2025 as Hunger Awarenes…
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming November 2025 as Hunger Awareness Month. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Name November Hunger Awareness Month
motions.summary: The council declared November 2025 as Hunger Awareness Month in Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: This is symbolic. No money, program, or rule comes with it, and nothing changes for residents.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda and to also include the “Conditions of Approval on Intersection Improvements”, provided by Staff, for Item 12.A. for the John Hancock Charter School West Campus. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Charter school gets intersection conditions
motions.summary: The council approved its routine consent agenda and attached staff conditions on intersection improvements to the John Hancock Charter School west campus item.
motions.impact: The consent items themselves are housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. The one item with teeth is the charter school's west campus, whose approval now carries city conditions about the nearby intersection.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Wastewater Master Plan and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Wastewater Master Plan and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP). Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Approve the long-range sewer plan
motions.summary: The city approved its wastewater master plan and the companion plan listing the future sewer projects that impact fees would help pay for.
motions.impact: No new charge shows up on your utility bill from this. The plan sets out which sewer projects the city expects to build and feeds into the fees charged on new construction.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Sweetwater #4 Community Reinvestment Area Project Area Plan, as Approved by the Redevelopment Agency of Eagle Mountain City, as the Official Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan for the Project Area and Directing that Notice of the Adoption be Given as Required by Statute
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Sweetwater #4 Community Reinvestment Area Project Area Plan, as Approved by the Redevelopment Agency of Eagle Mountain City, as the Official Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan for the Project Area and Directing that Notice of the Adoption be Given as Required by Statute. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Adopt the Sweetwater #4 redevelopment plan
motions.summary: The council made the Sweetwater #4 project area plan, already approved by the redevelopment agency, the city's official plan for that area.
motions.impact: If you don't live or own land near Sweetwater, you won't notice anything. For that area, this locks in the official plan the city will follow as redevelopment moves ahead.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Interlocal Cooperation Agreement between the Eagle Mountain Redevelopment Agency and Eagle Mountain City, Utah for the Collection and Remittance of Incremental Property Taxes Collected from Property Within the Sweetwater #4 Community Reinvestment Project Area
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Interlocal Cooperation Agreement between the Eagle Mountain Redevelopment Agency and Eagle Mountain City, Utah for the Collection and Remittance of Incremental Property Taxes Collected from Property Within the Sweetwater #4 Community Reinvestment Project Area. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Route Sweetwater #4 property taxes to the RDA
motions.summary: The city signed an agreement with its own redevelopment agency to collect the growth in property taxes from the Sweetwater #4 area and pass it along.
motions.impact: This doesn't change what you pay in property taxes. It's the plumbing that decides where tax money from that one project area goes, and it matters mainly to city staff and the redevelopment agency.
